rationale: g1+g2+g3 is the least-cost commitment: total capacity 460 MW covers demand+reserve (300 MW), and after losing the largest committed unit g3 (180 MW) the remaining 280 MW still covers demand (260 MW), so it is N-1 secure. The cheaper g1+g2+g4 (1410 USD) covers demand+reserve but fails N-1 (only 210 MW remains after losing g2), so it is infeasible.
